title: Allow removing node attributes
description:
## Issue:

Node attributes are adding a lot of text noise. This makes it harder to read the parsed tree itself.

Adding an option to remove them would make it easier to see what is going on with R parser.

This can be as simple as using regex at the end of the `xml_parse_data` (for a bit of overhead):

```{r}
pattern = paste0(
    " ",
    c("line1", "col1", "line2", "col2", "start", "end"),
    "=\"[[:digit:]]+\"",
    collapse = ""
    )

xmlparsedata::xml_parse_data(expr) |> gsub(pattern = pattern, replace = "")
```

## User story:

I am trying to understand how R is parsing different expressions to learn XPath for linting purpose.

The node attributes (`line`, `col`, `start`, and `end`) are adding quite lot of text noise and mental overhead to this.

Compare the following two snippets of the same `{x + 1}` expression:

```
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8" standalone="yes" ?>
<exprlist>
  <expr line1="1" col1="1" line2="1" col2="7" start="9" end="15">
    <OP-LEFT-BRACE line1="1" col1="1" line2="1" col2="1" start="9" end="9">{</OP-LEFT-BRACE>
    <expr line1="1" col1="2" line2="1" col2="6" start="10" end="14">
      <expr line1="1" col1="2" line2="1" col2="2" start="10" end="10">
        <SYMBOL line1="1" col1="2" line2="1" col2="2" start="10" end="10">x</SYMBOL>
      </expr>
      <OP-PLUS line1="1" col1="4" line2="1" col2="4" start="12" end="12">+</OP-PLUS>
      <expr line1="1" col1="6" line2="1" col2="6" start="14" end="14">
        <NUM_CONST line1="1" col1="6" line2="1" col2="6" start="14" end="14">1</NUM_CONST>
      </expr>
    </expr>
    <OP-RIGHT-BRACE line1="1" col1="7" line2="1" col2="7" start="15" end="15">}</OP-RIGHT-BRACE>
  </expr>
</exprlist>
```

```
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8" standalone="yes" ?>
<exprlist>
  <expr>
    <OP-LEFT-BRACE>{</OP-LEFT-BRACE>
    <expr>
      <expr>
        <SYMBOL>x</SYMBOL>
      </expr>
      <OP-PLUS>+</OP-PLUS>
      <expr>
        <NUM_CONST>1</NUM_CONST>
      </expr>
    </expr>
    <OP-RIGHT-BRACE>}</OP-RIGHT-BRACE>
  </expr>
</exprlist>
```

This makes comparing two parsed expressions much easier.

title: xml_parse_data could work even when keep.source=FALSE
description:
This is useful for cases where we only have the parsed input at hand & can't access the text source. We can still run XPath queries on the XML structure of the code, even if it doesn't give correct source metadata (basically as long as the query doesn't depend on whitespace or comments).

One simple approach would be to write the input to a tempfile, then use the current XML parser with a new option like `skip_metadata` to simply ignore line/column/start metadata.

e.g.

```r
dput(utils::read.table, tmp <- tempfile())
parse(tmp) |>
  xmlparsedata::xml_parse_data(skip_metadata = TRUE)
# gives a valid XML tree without attributes
```

Do you think that's in scope?

title: Missing documentation of start/end metadata
description:
I am trying to understand what these values mean, as it's apparently not something simple -- I had thought it's "character number in file" but I'm seeing `start` bigger than the file size.

```r
str <- "length(
  foo(
    x, y, z
  ) ==
  bar(
    a, b, c
  )
)"
writeLines(str, tmp <- tempfile())
nodes = parse(tmp) |>
  xmlparsedata::xml_parse_data() |>
  xml2::read_xml() |>
  xml_find_all("//*")
summary(as.integer(xml_attr(nodes, "start")))
#    Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max.    NA's 
#   13.00   30.00   47.00   52.39   77.00   97.00       1 
summary(as.integer(xml_attr(nodes, "end")))
#    Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max.    NA's 
#   18.00   42.00   54.00   58.79   80.00   97.00       1 
file.size(tmp)
# [1] 59
```

`?xml_parse_data` doesn't mention these at all

title: "\1" makes unparseable string in STR_CONST
description:
We are writing a linter to find non-regex regexes which involves examining the STR_CONST passed to functions like `gsub()`, `strsplit()`, etc:

https://github.com/r-lib/lintr/pull/1032

The linter threw an error in a rare usage here:

https://github.com/ggrothendieck/gsubfn/blob/66d52d9c0db277d39d3502d1db74911e8257fb64/R/gsubfn.R#L163

Where the relevant R code is:

```
strsplit(z, "\1")
```

the character literal here shows up in the XML parse data as:

```
<STR_CONST line1="1" col1="13" line2="1" col2="16" start="31" end="34">"\"</STR_CONST>
```

My guess is this is similar to #19... is there anything to do here besides resort to using the R code itself?

title: expr_as_xml helper?
description:
In exploratory / interactive work, it's often helpful to check quickly the XML representation of an expression.

I have a helper that looks like:

```r
expr_as_xml <- function(expr) {
  expr <- substitute(expr)
  if (is.character(expr)) {
    expr <- parse(text = expr)
  } else {
    expr <- parse(text = paste(deparse(expr), collapse = " "))
  }
  expr %>%
    xmlparsedata::xml_parse_data() %>%
    xml2::read_xml()
}
```

e.g.

```r
expr_as_xml(y[1, foo(2)]) |> as.character() |> writeLines()
```

gives

```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8" standalone="yes"?>
<exprlist>
  <expr line1="1" col1="1" line2="1" col2="12" start="14" end="25">
    <expr line1="1" col1="1" line2="1" col2="1" start="14" end="14">
      <SYMBOL line1="1" col1="1" line2="1" col2="1" start="14" end="14">y</SYMBOL>
    </expr>
    <OP-LEFT-BRACKET line1="1" col1="2" line2="1" col2="2" start="15" end="15">[</OP-LEFT-BRACKET>
    <expr line1="1" col1="3" line2="1" col2="3" start="16" end="16">
      <NUM_CONST line1="1" col1="3" line2="1" col2="3" start="16" end="16">1</NUM_CONST>
    </expr>
    <OP-COMMA line1="1" col1="4" line2="1" col2="4" start="17" end="17">,</OP-COMMA>
    <expr line1="1" col1="6" line2="1" col2="11" start="19" end="24">
      <expr line1="1" col1="6" line2="1" col2="8" start="19" end="21">
        <SYMBOL_FUNCTION_CALL line1="1" col1="6" line2="1" col2="8" start="19" end="21">foo</SYMBOL_FUNCTION_CALL>
      </expr>
      <OP-LEFT-PAREN line1="1" col1="9" line2="1" col2="9" start="22" end="22">(</OP-LEFT-PAREN>
      <expr line1="1" col1="10" line2="1" col2="10" start="23" end="23">
        <NUM_CONST line1="1" col1="10" line2="1" col2="10" start="23" end="23">2</NUM_CONST>
      </expr>
      <OP-RIGHT-PAREN line1="1" col1="11" line2="1" col2="11" start="24" end="24">)</OP-RIGHT-PAREN>
    </expr>
    <OP-RIGHT-BRACKET line1="1" col1="12" line2="1" col2="12" start="25" end="25">]</OP-RIGHT-BRACKET>
  </expr>
</exprlist>
```

This is quite helpful for developing linters, so I first thought to add it to lintr, but maybe it's more useful in xmlparsedata instead?

The only trouble is xml2 is Suggests, maybe a version like this would be more useful?

```r
expr_as_xml <- function(expr, parse_xml = requireNamespace("xml2", quietly = TRUE)) {
  expr <- substitute(expr)
  if (is.character(expr)) {
    expr <- parse(text = expr)
  } else {
    expr <- parse(text = paste(deparse(expr), collapse = " "))
  }
  xml_string <- xml_parse_data(expr)
  if (!parse_xml) {
    return(xml_string)
  }
  xml2::read_xml(xml_string)
}
```

WDYT?

title: Move `master` branch to `main`
description:
The `master` branch of this repository will soon be renamed to `main`, as part of a coordinated change across several GitHub organizations (including, but not limited to: [tidyverse](https://github.com/tidyverse), [r-lib](https://github.com/r-lib), [tidymodels](https://github.com/tidymodels), and [sol-eng](https://github.com/sol-eng)). We anticipate this will happen by the end of September 2021.

That will be preceded by a release of the [usethis package](https://usethis.r-lib.org), which will gain some functionality around detecting and adapting to a renamed default branch. There will also be a blog post at the time of this `master` --> `main` change.

The purpose of this issue is to:

* Help us firm up the list of targetted repositories
* Make sure all maintainers are aware of what's coming
* Give us an issue to close when the job is done
* Give us a place to put advice for collaborators re: how to adapt

*message id: euphoric_snowdog*

title: Form feed (\f = rawToChar(as.raw(0x0c))) produces invalid XML?
description:
I was parsing some R source code and ran into this:

https://github.com/wch/r-source/blob/e7eb333dd43be7f7e5ce12d1c31d1934c6b79ac9/tests/reg-packages.R#L232

MRE:

```
xml <- xmlparsedata::xml_parse_data(parse(text = "cat('\f')\n"))
cat(xml)
# <exprlist>
# <expr line1="1" col1="1" line2="1" col2="8" start="10" end="17">
# <expr line1="1" col1="1" line2="1" col2="3" start="10" end="12">
# <SYMBOL_FUNCTION_CALL line1="1" col1="1" line2="1" col2="3" start="10" end="12">cat</SYMBOL_FUNCTION_CALL>
# </expr>
# <OP-LEFT-PAREN line1="1" col1="4" line2="1" col2="4" start="13" end="13">(</OP-LEFT-PAREN>
# <expr line1="1" col1="5" line2="1" col2="7" start="14" end="16">
# <STR_CONST line1="1" col1="5" line2="1" col2="7" start="14" end="16">'
#                                                                       '</STR_CONST>
# </expr>
# <OP-RIGHT-PAREN line1="1" col1="8" line2="1" col2="8" start="17" end="17">)</OP-RIGHT-PAREN>
# </expr>
# </exprlist>

xml2::read_xml(xml)
# Error in read_xml.raw(charToRaw(enc2utf8(x)), "UTF-8", ..., as_html = as_html,  : 
#   PCDATA invalid Char value 12 [9]
```

I'm not sure if this is an `xmlparsedata` issue or a `read_xml` one, but starting here. FWIW this site lists the HTML equivalent as ``; that said, a direct fix doesn't seem to solve the issue:

```
xml <- gsub("\f", "", xml, fixed = TRUE)
xml2::read_xml(xml)
# Error in read_xml.raw(charToRaw(enc2utf8(x)), "UTF-8", ..., as_html = as_html,  : 
#   xmlParseCharRef: invalid xmlChar value 12 [9]
```

[This Q&A](https://stackoverflow.com/a/19633698/3576984) suggests there's no simple way to deal with the issue... and looking at how `\n` is dealt with, it's less clear `xmlparsedata` should be doing something here...

`\v` has the same issue, at a glance, as I'm sure a few other weird characters from the ASCII table do as well...

title: R 4.0 raw string support
description:
R 4.0 introduces raw string in the form of `r"(hello, "world")"` (see https://stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-devel/library/base/html/Quotes.html).

For the following code:

```r
x <- r"(hello, "world")"
```

`xmlparsedata::xml_parse_data()` produces the following XML output (formatted):

```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8" standalone="yes" ?>
<exprlist>
  <expr line1="1" col1="1" line2="1" col2="24" start="26" end="49">
    <expr line1="1" col1="1" line2="1" col2="1" start="26" end="26">
      <SYMBOL line1="1" col1="1" line2="1" col2="1" start="26" end="26">x</SYMBOL>
    </expr>
    <LEFT_ASSIGN line1="1" col1="3" line2="1" col2="4" start="28" end="29"><-</LEFT_ASSIGN>
    <expr line1="1" col1="6" line2="1" col2="24" start="31" end="49">
      <STR_CONST line1="1" col1="6" line2="1" col2="24" start="31" end="49">"hello, "world")</STR_CONST>
    </expr>
  </expr>
</exprlist>
```

It looks like the value of  the `STR_CONST` node is not consistent to work with because it omits the opening `(` and closing `"` but keeps closing `)`.

title: Support lambda syntax
description:
In the R-devel, the pipe `|>` and lambda `\(x) x + 1` syntax are introduced. I take a look at their parse data to find if anything is broken here.

The parse data looks good but `xml_parse_data` produces invalid XML since `\\` is a new token and is not allowed in XML node name.

```r
> e <- quote(\(x) x + 1)                                                                                                                                                                                                            

> e                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 
function(x) x + 1

> e <- parse(text = "\\(x) x + 1")                                                                                                                                                                                                  

> pd <- getParseData(e)                                                                                                                                                                                                             

> pd                                                                                                                                                                                                                                
   line1 col1 line2 col2 id parent          token terminal text
14     1    1     1   10 14      0           expr    FALSE     
1      1    1     1    1  1     14         '\\\\'     TRUE   \\
2      1    2     1    2  2     14            '('     TRUE    (
3      1    3     1    3  3     14 SYMBOL_FORMALS     TRUE    x
4      1    4     1    4  4     14            ')'     TRUE    )
12     1    6     1   10 12     14           expr    FALSE     
6      1    6     1    6  6      8         SYMBOL     TRUE    x
8      1    6     1    6  8     12           expr    FALSE     
7      1    8     1    8  7     12            '+'     TRUE    +
9      1   10     1   10  9     10      NUM_CONST     TRUE    1
10     1   10     1   10 10     12           expr    FALSE     

> xml <- xml_parse_data(e)                                                                                                                                                                                                          

> xml2::read_xml(xml)                                                                                                                                                                                                               
Error in read_xml.raw(charToRaw(enc2utf8(x)), "UTF-8", ..., as_html = as_html,  : 
  StartTag: invalid element name [68]
Backtrace:
1: read_xml.raw(charToRaw(enc2utf8(x)), "UTF-8", ..., as_html = as_html, 
2: read_xml.character(xml)
3: xml2::read_xml(xml)
```

It looks like we need to extend the current `xml_parse_token_map` to include `'\\\\'`.

Since the new syntax are still experimental in r-devel and may be subject to change, I'm not sure when we should consider to support it.

title: "a = 1" parsing gives invalid xml text (R 3.6.1)
description:
Hi. There's an issue running some xmlparsedata-dependent code within the tests for `lintr` on R-3.6.1 (https://github.com/jimhester/lintr/issues/384) and I think it relates to `xmlparsedata`.

If I clone the current master (https://github.com/r-lib/xmlparsedata/commit/99a30b1a0d8b60600b6ffb4e4f10b6591560515b) for `xmlparsedata` and run in an R-3.6.1 environment:

```
# from xmlparsedata directory
devtools::load_all()
devtools::test() # no errors are thrown for the existing tests
```

```
xml2::read_xml(xml_parse_data(parse(text = "a = 1", keep.source = TRUE)))
Error in doc_parse_raw(x, encoding = encoding, base_url = base_url, as_html = as_html,  : 
  Opening and ending tag mismatch: expr line 8 and equal_assign [76]
```

```
cat(xml_parse_data(parse(text = "a = 1", keep.source = TRUE), pretty = TRUE), file = "")

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"standalone="yes" ?>
<exprlist>
  <equal_assign line1="1" col1="1" line2="1" col2="5" start="7" end="11">
    <expr line1="1" col1="1" line2="1" col2="1" start="7" end="7">
      <SYMBOL line1="1" col1="1" line2="1" col2="1" start="7" end="7">a</SYMBOL>
    </expr>
    <EQ_ASSIGN line1="1" col1="3" line2="1" col2="3" start="9" end="9">=</EQ_ASSIGN>
    <expr line1="1" col1="5" line2="1" col2="5" start="11" end="11">
      <NUM_CONST line1="1" col1="5" line2="1" col2="5" start="11" end="11">1</NUM_CONST>
    </equal_assign>
  </expr>
</exprlist>
```

The xml that is produced isn't legal: `equal_assign` is interleaved with one of the `expr`s.
